parallel.requirements: The parallel run recognized the clean-room requirement to recreate `walk` solely from observed binary and bundled documentation behavior.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent split behavioral exploration across seven concurrent children and kept implementation scaffolding with itself.
parallel.implementation: It initialized a Go module, preserved the original binary for comparison, and wrote `term.go`, `renderer.go`, `input.go`, and `main.go` skeleton files.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent had not integrated a complete UI core or final build pipeline before closure; the artifact remained incomplete and failed compilation.
parallel.verification: Verification was mostly planned or exploratory through child probes and a diff harness; the official evaluator later reported `compile_failed`.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Multiple child probes were still active, implementation was scaffolding-level, and the completed official evaluation had zero passing tests.

serial.requirements: The serial run recognized the same clean-room reverse-engineering task and the restriction against source lookup or wrapping.
serial.plan_and_ownership: The serial attempt stayed single-agent, using its own PTY observation harness instead of delegating specialized concurrent probes.
serial.implementation: It focused on local behavioral probing under `/tmp/obs` and did not produce a complete compiled replacement in the submitted workspace.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial artifact lacked a coherent built reimplementation and was evaluated as a compile failure.
serial.verification: It used interactive PTY captures and exploratory checks, but no final evaluator-aligned build success was established before closure.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The serial trajectory also timed out with no passing tests, making the official pair outcome a same-failure result.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent decomposed the reverse-engineering work into seven live specialist children while retaining scaffold implementation work.

comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used broad concurrent specialist probing; serial used one continuous local investigation path.

comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote a local observation driver under `/tmp/obs`, with no separate child handoff or helper namespace conflict.

comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also timed out under the same official budget, but without background child work.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had additional concurrent-management overhead and active children at closure; serial's failure was a single-agent timeout.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official records are not discordant: both parallel and serial failed compilation with zero passing tests. The parallel trajectory shows an adverse helper-leakage episode during concurrent probing, while the serial trajectory avoids that specific contamination, but both attempts remained incomplete or uncompilable at official evaluation.
parallel_contributors: Concurrent child probes contaminated shared `/tmp` helper files and forced failed imports and rework during exploration.
The parent still had active child work and only scaffold-level Go implementation before closure.
serial_contributors: The serial run avoided child-agent helper contamination by staying single-agent and using a scoped `/tmp/obs` helper.
It nevertheless timed out and failed official compilation with no passing tests.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel wrote more visible Go scaffolding, while serial focused more on observation; neither reached a complete compiling implementation.

candidates.reason: The parent retained implementation ownership and wrote Go scaffold files; implementation was incomplete, not ownerless.
There were no completed independently owned components requiring an unassigned integration step.
Final assembly was not a ready component set left unowned; the implementation itself remained incomplete.
The parent was acting as end-to-end owner; failure was incomplete execution and contamination, not an ownerless pipeline.
No single mandatory preflight gate blocked all productive work; parent scaffolding proceeded while probes ran.
The investigators overlapped and were not completed as a clean first phase before all implementation began.
The trace shows broad probing and incomplete implementation, but not a separately evidenced indispensable path starved by auxiliary work.
Seven children and timeout are screening signals, but the distinct realized coordination consequence is helper artifact leakage, and serial also timed out.
No single child had a demonstrably overbroad scope relative to siblings with its own unfinished indispensable deliverable.
Child briefs included the target, restrictions, harness context, and specific probe areas; the failure was not omission of a known task requirement.
No independently implemented components diverged at an omitted API or file contract; the concrete event was temp-helper leakage.
There is no known finding lost through summary or transfer that made a receiver repeat work.
No returned handoff was available but too bulky to reduce before a decision point.
No receiver used a superseded report or workspace description as current state.
No incompatible child reports reached the parent and remained unadjudicated; the issue was concrete helper contamination.
The parent did not present the whole task as complete; it explicitly said it would wait for agent findings before implementing the UI core.
There is no replacement or retry child that lacked inherited checkpoints and repeated prior work as the decisive event.

candidates.reason: No parent action explicitly stopped or cancelled an active child before a needed result; process timeout alone is insufficient.
No complete promotable candidate or mutually compatible component set existed ready for final placement.
No child implementation was integrated after relevant integrated verification without a post-merge check.

The observed child helper failures led to helper-name adaptation; there was no separate required failed scope left without takeover.

The parent inspected active task status and the retained concrete consequence is helper contamination, not blind waiting over available results.
There were no competing implementation files claiming overlapping final behavior; the collision was in temporary helper artifacts.
No final source or configuration file was co-edited by live agents; temporary helper consumption is classified more specifically.

No broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion replaced multiple final workspace outputs from another agent.
Generic shared helper writes existed, but the proven adverse event is leaked helper consumption, making Artifact Leakage more specific.

candidates.realized_consequence: Parallel probe helpers in `/tmp` were consumed as shared state by other live agents, causing failed imports, failed probe batches, and rework to unique helper names during observation.
candidates.near_match_reason: The broader write label is wrong because the concrete adverse event is consumption of leaked helper artifacts, not just unisolated writes.
